feedback: For public SDK examples, never include the phrase 'live secret token'. Do not apply this rule to internal incident runbooks.
violation_output: The README uses a live secret token in the example.
compliant_output: The README uses a redacted example token.
excluded_output: The internal runbook records the live secret token for incident response.

feedback: For consumer-facing launch copy, avoid the phrase 'clinically proven'. Do not apply this rule to internal evidence dossiers.
violation_output: Our formula is clinically proven to work.
compliant_output: The formula is designed for everyday use.
excluded_output: The internal dossier evaluates whether the product is clinically proven.

feedback: In onboarding UI, do not use the label 'delete account' for an action that can be undone. Do not apply this rule to destructive settings.
excluded_output: This destructive settings page includes a Delete account action.

feedback: In executive summaries, never describe the phrase 'causal proof' as a conclusion from correlation alone. Do not apply this rule to randomized trial protocols.
violation_output: This correlation is causal proof of the intervention effect.
compliant_output: The two measures were associated in this sample.
excluded_output: The randomized trial protocol defines evidence needed for causal proof.
